In this article LOW Follow your favorite stocks CREATE FREE ACCOUNT watch now VIDEO 6:58 06:58 Lowe’s posts strong online sales, raises outlook despite slow housing market Squawk Box Lowe's on Wednesday posted strong quarterly results and raised its full-year outlook as the company said it saw strength among professional shoppers. The company said comparable sales grew 1.8% for the fiscal third quarter, driven by a 17.4% increase in online sales and "solid" performance in pro and home services sales. Net sales rose to $22.76 billion. Because of the strength, Lowe's now said it expects full-year sales of roughly $92.5 billion, up from a previous projection of $92 billion. It also expects comparable sales to be up 0.5%, compared with previous guidance of flat. CEO Marvin Ellison told CNBC that the company is focused on growing despite economic headwinds and a sluggish housing market. He said Lowe's posted its sixth straight quarterly comparable sales increase and saw particular strength in appliances, which saw its largest revenue growth in five years. "We believe irrespective of the macro environment we're in, we're going to take share because there's a lot of share out there that we can go and get, and we're going to be aggressive to go and get that share," Ellison told CNBC. Lowe's also reported a pretax benefit of approximately $250 million from tariff refunds during the quarter, which contributed a 34-cent boost to earnings per share. Ellison said the company plans to use those funds to enhance the customer experience and bring value to shoppers. He added that do-it-yourself customers and pro shoppers are not investing in major renovation projects but are instead spending on repair and maintenance projects. "We are giving those pros what they need," he said. "We're able to improve our fulfillment capabilities and our pro loyalty program." Here's how the company performed in its fiscal third quarter compared with what Wall Street was expecting, based on a survey of analysts by LSEG: Earnings per share: $3.10 adjusted, it was not immediately clear if that compared to the $2.88 expected Revenue: $22.76 billion vs. $22.41 billion expected For the quarter ended Oct. 30, Lowe's reported net income of $1.67 billion, or $2.98 per share, compared with $1.62 billion, or $2.88 per share, the year prior. The home improvement retailer has previously said it's seeing "pressure" on spending on projects, especially as consumers are stretched thin by inflation and macroeconomic uncertainty. The company is also battling a slower housing market and higher mortgage rates. Ellison previously told CNBC he expects consumers to remain cautious through the end of the year. Lowe's executives said on a call with analysts Wednesday that the company is continuing to battle high fuel costs, which they said accelerated through the third quarter. CFO Brandon Sink said diesel prices are currently around $6 per gallon, up about 15% overall compared to what the company saw in the second quarter. "So we're trying to continue to manage that, balance that, and we're reflecting that into our Q4 guide," Sink said. Ellison told CNBC the company remains optimistic about consumer spending this holiday season and that November sales are in line with expectations so far. headlines.article_text: Tech outage Costco panic buying Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu In this article COST Follow your favorite stocks CREATE FREE ACCOUNT A shopper leaves a Costco store in Bayonne, New Jersey, Oct. 2, 2026. Gary Hershorn | Corbis News | Getty Images A series of tech outages has consumers stocking up on emergency supplies. Costco sales are seeing a lift because of it, according to research firm Mizuho. In the final week of October, Mizuho estimates Costco's U.S. comparable sales, excluding gasoline, rose 11% to 12%, up from the normal 6% to 7% the first three weeks in October. Costco reported an 8.1% increase for the month. The firm said the stronger pace is continuing through November as 21 of the 26 high-ticket generators it tracked on Costco's website sold out as of Sunday night. Shares of Costco were roughly flat-to-lower in Wednesday morning trading around $1,107 apiece. "Consumer anxiety following the Microsoft Outlook outage, the ground stoppage for all U.S. airline flights, and apocalyptic concerns flaring up across social media have all contributed to increased emergency prep sales at COST," said Mizuho analyst David Bellinger in a research note Monday. Bellinger will appear on CNBC's "The Exchange" during the 1pm hour. The stockpiling intensified from a series of recent disruptions . Microsoft's Outlook and Teams outage on Thursday, the Federal Aviation Administration halted departures nation-wide on Friday. A separate software outage at JPMorgan Chase Monday caused banking transaction delays while a system outage delayed United Airlines flights Monday. The National Security Agency on Tuesday said the spy agency's communication network went down temporarily. The various outages appear to come amid a rush to recover software vulnerabilities uncovered by AI tools and officials are saying there's no reason for panic. Still, on TikTok and other social media platforms, posts urging people to stock up on food and supplies are gaining significant traction. Mizuho raised its price target on Costco to $1,150 from $1,100 and kept its buy-equivalent outperform rating. The firm said U.S. comparable sales could grow more than 10% in November. Mizuho also sees Walmart 's Sam's Club benefiting from emergency preparedness sales as shoppers fill up their pantries, and for Home Depot and Lowe's as they buy home improvement emergency supplies. At Costco, Mizuho will be watching whether the surge brought in new members sign-ups when the warehouse retailer reports its first quarter of fiscal 2027 on Dec. 10. headlines.article_text: Anthropic IPO: AI lab considers increasing offering Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu Key Points Anthropic is considering upsizing its IPO, according to people familiar with the details. The AI lab is expected to set its final IPO price after market close on Wednesday. The stock is set to begin trading on the Nasdaq under the ticker symbol "ANT" on Thursday. In this article ANT Follow your favorite stocks CREATE FREE ACCOUNT Anthropic Co-founder and CEO Dario Amodei speaks during INBOUND 2025 Powered by HubSpot at Moscone Center on Sept. 4, 2025 in San Francisco, California. Chance Yeh | Getty Images Anthropic is considering upsizing its IPO, people familiar with the details told CNBC, as the artificial intelligence lab weighs setting the price well above $80. The company closed its order books and locked in total demand on Tuesday, setting the stage for the Claude creator's eagerly awaited Nasdaq listing. Institutional demand for the offering is around $400 billion, while retail demand is approaching $100 billion, according to the people, who asked not to be named because they were not authorized to speak publicly. The orders are indications of interest and are not binding. All of the details are subject to change, and Anthropic will make final decisions on Wednesday afternoon, the people said. Anthropic is expected to set its final IPO price after market close on Wednesday. Demand for the offering is higher than it was for Elon Musk's SpaceX , even though the rocket maker had a bigger market offering. SpaceX debuted on the Nasdaq in June in by far the biggest IPO on record, ultimately raising $85.7 billion. The AI lab said last week that it would offer 825 million shares in the IPO at a price range between $70 and $78 per share, which would net up to $64.35 billion at the high end of that range. A representative for Anthropic declined to comment. Anthropic's listing is a major test for the AI industry, which has experienced a set of recent shocks, including a dramatic backlash that was felt at the polls in the midterm elections and last week's ouster of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang . The market was already jittery on concerns that rising interest rates will make debt unaffordable for many data center developers and neoclouds. Tech's biggest companies have significant exposure to Anthropic, whether as an investor, partner or customer. Amazon and Google both own stakes valued at over $100 billion, and a group of tech companies, including Google, Microsoft , Nvidia and Advanced Micro Devices agreed to collectively invest $26 billion in the IPO. Anthropic, meanwhile, is a buyer of costly systems from Nvidia, Google, Amazon and AMD. "We have to make sure that all the risks, all the ways that things can go wrong with this technology, we very carefully address those risks as we bring the benefits and as we have a viable business at the same time." Amodei co-founded Anthropic alongside a handful of other researchers less than six years ago, after the group collectively defected from OpenAI. The company is best known for developing a family of AI models called Claude , and it primarily sells its products and services to other businesses. Anthropic has been racing to maintain an edge over OpenAI and Google in the enterprise market, and it experienced a period of explosive growth in 2026, driven largely by the popularity of its AI coding tool, Claude Code. OpenAI has confidentially filed for an IPO and has said a debut is likely in 2027. For the nine months ended Sept. 30, Anthropic said it generated $33.24 billion in revenue, up roughly 1,200% from the same period last year, according to its prospectus. The company reported a $104 billion net loss during the nine-month period, though most of that was due to the change in fair value of convertible notes and derivative liabilities. Anthropic lost $25.1 billion over the same stretch in 2025, the filing said. Anthropic said in an amended filing that its run-rate revenue was roughly $81 billion at the end of October, up $10 billion from the previous month. The company has faced plenty of challenges during its meteoric rise over its positions on safety, regulation and national security, leading to two high-profile disputes with the U.S. government this year. Its prospectus included more than 90 pages of risk factors for investors to consider ahead of its IPO. "Our aim is to help humankind chart a safe course through this technological evolution, open new frontiers of discovery, and bring forth an age of miracles," Anthropic's co-founders wrote in the company's prospectus. "Everyone who owns our stock, whether an institution or an individual, becomes part of that effort."
